comm_act_intro: Community Councils carry out a wide range of activities that span generations.
comm_act_list:
• Disaster preparedness & safety: Organizing and participating in area-wide disaster drills, preparing evacuation-shelter manuals, disaster imagination games (DIG)
  • Crime prevention: Forming blue-light patrol teams, creating safety maps, watching over children
  • Children's events: Kite-flying, mochi-pounding, walk rallies, sports meets, and more
  • Community exchange: Summer festivals, fireworks shows, music festivals
  • Senior support: Wellness salons, Orange Cafés (dementia cafés), neighbourhood helper teams
  • Digital support: Smartphone classes
comm_act_note: The city groups local issues into four areas — disaster preparedness, crime prevention, welfare, and exchange — and each council plans its projects along these lines.
comm_base_p: As the name "○○ Elementary School District" implies, the elementary school district is the geographic foundation of each Community Council. School districts serve as units of social cohesion, and Community Councils use this framework to cultivate horizontal connections among residents.
comm_card_list: 📋 The five Community Councils of the Shinooka area
comm_club_p: After-school childcare clubs for children of dual-income families are also organized on a school-district basis and operate in coordination with Community Councils and PTAs. After the reorganization, a club is to be set up inside each of Tokadai Higashi and Tokadai Nishi elementary schools (FAQ).
comm_consider1:
Schools and community ties
Schools bring together not only children but also parents and local residents. Events such as sports days, school presentations and evacuation drills are also occasions for people of different generations to meet. For this reason, school mergers are often described as affecting not only the learning environment but also how local people are connected.
comm_consider2:
Points raised when organizations cover a wider area
A wider area can make it easier to pool people and funds, and lets residents across a larger area work together. On the other hand, taking part can become harder once activities go beyond the circle of people who know each other, and attachment to the former school district may fade. Which side comes out stronger is generally said to depend on how the transition is handled and how residents take part.
comm_consider3:
How the transition proceeds
When local organizations merge, the timing, how activities are handed over, and how residents are informed and consulted become the main issues. In the Shinooka district, the five councils are to be reorganized into two, targeting fiscal 2029, and how the merger proceeds will be decided through future discussions. At the 2025 briefings and public comment process, residents also voiced concern about the future of the local community.

comm_cs_p1: Each school in Komaki City has a School Management Council (Community School). This is a forum where parents and local residents can share opinions on the school's educational policies and operations — an important institution connecting Community Councils with schools.
comm_cs_p2: It creates opportunities for local adults to participate in classroom support, read-alouds, and career education, and to share school challenges with the wider community.
comm_def_p1: A Community Council is an organization voluntarily formed by local residents based on the elementary school district. Groups such as neighborhood associations, PTAs, senior clubs, sports clubs, and welfare commissioners participate across organizational lines to discuss local issues and revitalize community life.
comm_def_p2: In Komaki City, Community Councils have been established in 14 of the city's 16 elementary school districts (as of April 2026). The five elementary school districts in the Shinooka area (Shinooka, Hikarigaoka, Oshiro, Momogaoka, and Sue) each have their own council.
comm_events_h2: Community council events<small>地域協議会のイベント案内</small>
comm_events_lead: Event listings for community councils, published by Komaki City (🔄 fetched automatically every day). They cover all 16 elementary school districts in the city, so events from the five Shinooka-area councils are marked and shown first.
comm_fac_p: The gymnasiums, sports fields, and pools of each school are used daily by local residents for community sports and as disaster bases (evacuation sites). Community members also participate in school events such as sports meets and learning fairs, making schools serve as the public "face" of the community.
comm_leg_bonote_p: A tradition of offering old martial-art forms with staffs and other tools at shrine festivals. Okusa Bo-no-te (Shinkage school) is offered at the festival of Okusa Hachiman Shrine and Noguchi Bo-no-te (Genji Ten school) at that of Noguchi Shinmei Shrine, both every year on the second Sunday of October. Both are intangible folk cultural properties designated by the city. They died out for a time after the war, but local people formed preservation societies, revived them and still pass them on.
comm_leg_budou_p: Grapes are widely grown alongside peaches in Kamisue, Takane, Okusa and nearby. Fifth graders at Hikarigaoka Elementary School pick grapes with the help of local grape farmers. The local “Eastern District Specialty PR Team” and grape farmers have held a parent-and-child Christmas wreath workshop using Komaki grapes, and at a local-produce cooking session people made grape juice from grape skins.
comm_leg_cochin_p: The city presents Nagoya Cochin chicken as a specialty of the eastern district. According to the Shinooka Karuta, it was bred by a former Owari domain samurai who moved to Ikenouchi, started keeping chickens and crossed breeds again and again. In connection with “Nagoya Cochin Day” on 10 March, a local group holds sessions in Toryou Junior High School’s cooking room to make hikizuri-nabe, a local dish. At a market in the east, food-truck dishes using Nagoya Cochin quickly sold out.
comm_leg_fest_p: At the Ikenouchi festival a preservation society keeps up festival music, playing a piece called “Okagura” on flutes and drums, and there is also the “mikomai”, danced to it with bells and fans. At Fukugonji Temple in Okusa, a fire-walking ritual is held in midwinter: people follow the head priest across burning fire to purify body and mind. At the Sue district summer festival, Sue Elementary School’s wadaiko drum club performed.
comm_leg_hist_h: Oyama Temple Ruins and Chigo Shrine
comm_leg_hist_p: In Oyama are the ruins of Oyamamine Shofukuji, a temple thought to have been founded in the late 7th century: the “Oyama Temple Ruins”. It once flourished so much that people said “Enryakuji on Mt. Hiei in the west, Oyama Temple in the east”, but it was burned in an attack in the mid-12th century. It is a national historic site — one of only two in the city, with Komakiyama. Chigo Shrine to its south is said to have been built to console the spirits of two temple boys who died in the attack, and its approach, lined with nearly 100 cherry trees, is a well-known cherry-blossom spot. The exhibition design (March 2025) for the city’s Komaki History Discovery Museum (こまき歴史発見館), now open on the 4th floor of Lapio with free admission, planned a corner on the ruins showing the pagoda’s foundation stones life-size on the floor.
comm_leg_hotaru_p: The Oyama River crosses the east and is a large river where five streams, including the Ikeshita and Shinzo, meet. Upstream, the “Firefly Village” (Oyama-higashi) has been laid out as a rest area, and from early to mid-June Genji fireflies — now rarely seen — fly about. This scene too is one of the “Beautiful Aichi Landscape Resources”. Shinooka Elementary School raises fireflies from larvae and releases them into the Oyama River.
comm_leg_kama_h: Ancient kilns and the history of pottery
comm_leg_kama_p: From the 7th to the 11th century, the Shinooka district was, together with the Sanage kilns, a centre of pottery making (ceramics) in the Owari region. More than 110 kiln sites have been found, known as the Shinooka Ancient Kiln Sites. They were half-underground “ana-gama” tunnel kilns, dug as narrow trenches into hill slopes and roofed with clay; Sue ware was fired in the 7th–8th centuries and ash-glazed ware from the late 9th century. Characters written on Sue ware from Shinooka Kiln No. 78 closely resemble those on Sue ware found at the Fujiwara capital in Nara, showing that Shinooka’s vessels travelled as far as Nara. The exhibition design (March 2025) for the city’s Komaki History Discovery Museum (こまき歴史発見館), now open on the 4th floor of Lapio with free admission, also planned a corner on the Shinooka kilns where visitors can touch pottery shards.
comm_leg_karuta_p: A local karuta card set on Shinooka Elementary School’s website. It turns the area’s history, ways of life and nature into 36 pairs of picture cards and explanation cards. Topics include how Shinooka Village came about, fireflies on the Oyama River, climbing kilns, the Battle of Komaki and Nagakute, bo-no-te, festival music and mikomai, peaches and grapes, Nagoya Cochin and bracken.
comm_leg_lead: Apart from the schools, the eastern district has traditions, festivals and local specialties that local people have handed down. They are the area’s heritage, and they go on even when the schools are reorganized.
comm_leg_mame_p: The endangered Mamenashi grows wild in Okusa. It is one of the “Tokai hill-zone plants” found only in the hills of the Tokai region, and the “Tara Mamenashi Village” has a walking path and signboards. Local groups hold viewing sessions in spring when it flowers and in autumn when it fruits.
comm_leg_matsuri_p: A summer event of Tokadai New Town, held every year in Tokadai Central Park, with bon-odori dancing, a flea market and food stalls. The 40th was held on 25–26 July 2026.
comm_leg_momo_p: The peach orchards on the eastern hills gave “Tokadai” (“peach-blossom heights”) its name, and the landscape (Kamisue) is one of Aichi Prefecture’s “Beautiful Aichi Landscape Resources”. “Shinooka peaches” are known nationwide for their large, very sweet fruit. They have been grown in Kamisue, Takane, Okusa and nearby for about 80 years, and at Toryou Junior High School students cook with eastern peaches grown by a parent.
comm_leg_more: This site’s view on how to carry on these traditions after the schools close (not the city’s view) is in In-depth review: “Carrying on the existing schools’ legacy”.
comm_leg_ondo_p: The “Shinooka Ondo”, also called the “Shin-Shinooka Ondo”, is a local song bearing the Shinooka name, loved as a bon-odori staple. A recording posted on a video-sharing site shows that it was released as a record. Its origins could not be confirmed from published materials.
comm_leg_src: Sources: Komaki City Board of Education, Cultural Properties Division (bo-no-te); Komaki City “Komaki Kentei: questions and explanations” (4th and 6th) and the exhibition design for the history and folklore exhibition facility (provisional name, March 2025) (Oyama Temple Ruins, ancient kilns, peaches); Komaki City page on the “Beautiful Aichi Landscape Resources” (Oyama Temple Ruins, peach orchards, Firefly Village); Komaki City “Eastern District Development News” and Eastern District trial activity pages (Tokadai Festival, grapes, Nagoya Cochin, Mamenashi); Shinooka Elementary School website, “Shinooka Karuta”; the schools’ diaries; a record recording posted on a video-sharing site (Shin-Shinooka Ondo). Please check the latest dates with each group or organizer.
comm_list_intro: All five elementary school districts in the Shinooka area have a Community Council, and all five were certified by the city on April 1, 2020. The oldest, Sue Elementary District, was founded in 2014 and has over a decade of activity behind it.

comm_pf_link_about: About the Eastern District Town Development Platform (Komaki City, Japanese)
comm_pf_link_form: Registration form (logo form linked by the city, Japanese)
comm_pf_p1: A space the city opened, based on the Eastern District Development Concept it adopted in March 2022, for people involved in the east’s town development to connect. Residents, businesses, schools and other educational institutions, and the city register, share information and find partners to act with. The city likens it to a station platform: not a destination, but a place where people meet on their way to the next step.
comm_pf_p2: Anyone interested can register, not only people who live in the eastern district. After agreeing to the terms and registering, you receive from the city’s Eastern District Development Office an invitation to an online space on LINE OpenChat, and notices of in-person gatherings such as discussion meetings, workshops and town-development seminars.
comm_pf_src: Source: Komaki City, “東部まちづくりプラットフォームとは？”. Rewritten by this site after reading the city’s page; not the city’s own wording.
comm_qa1_a: The city has announced a policy of reorganizing to 2 Community Councils by FY2029, but how the integration proceeds and how each event will be handled will be determined through consultations with residents and the individual councils. At this point, many details about how activities will be handed over remain undecided, and it is hoped that a forum will be provided for residents' voices to be reflected.
comm_qa1_q: What will happen to current activities when the councils are reduced to two?
comm_qa2_a: Schools have served as hubs for community events, disaster preparedness, sports, and childcare. School consolidation means the number of these hubs will change, but the city has declared a policy of continuing community use of closed school facilities, so gymnasiums and sports fields are expected to remain available. How to rebuild the community itself will need to be discussed with residents taking the lead.
comm_qa2_q: Won't community bonds weaken if the local school disappears?
comm_qa3_a: They won't disappear. New School Management Councils (Community Schools) will be organized in each of the 4 new schools after reorganization (Tokadai Higashi Elementary, Tokadai Nishi Elementary, Tokadai Higashi Junior High, Tokadai Nishi Junior High). However, how to carry on the relationships and activities cultivated by each current school's Community School depends on future consultations. A joint school management council of the eight schools is planned for December 2026 (“Shinooka School Reorganization News” No. 4).
comm_qa3_q: Will Community School activities disappear with the school consolidation?
comm_qa4_a: Events that each Community Council has organized over many years (disaster drills, children's events, local festivals, etc.) are activities carried out by local residents. Even after the councils are integrated, continuation is possible based on the will and consensus of local residents, but the specific form will be at the discretion of the new post-reorganization councils. No official policy has yet been announced.
comm_qa4_q: What will happen to local events that each community has independently continued?
